question: Who has validated an AI system for lung cancer screening in a real screening cohort?

steps.step: 2. query rewrite (Haiku) then embedding search, k=15
steps.hypothetical_abstract: This prospective, multicenter cohort study will enroll 12,000 adults aged 50-80 with at least 20 pack-years of smoking who are undergoing annual low-dose CT lung cancer screening at six academic and community screening programs. Each baseline and follow-up scan will be read independently by board-certified radiologists using Lung-RADS v2022 and by a locked, pre-specified deep learning system that outputs nodule detection and per-patient malignancy risk, with radiologists blinded to AI output, and ground truth will be established by histopathology or at least 24 months of follow-up. Primary metrics will be AUC, sensitivity, specificity, and positive predictive value for screen-detected cancer at 1 and 2 years, with secondary outcomes comparing false-positive and recall rates, interval cancer detection, reader time, and performance across sex, race, and scanner vendor subgroups using 95% bootstr

steps.step: 5. grade candidates with Haiku, batches of 10

review:
**1) Validated studies (cohort, size, task, result)**

- Ledda et al., BioMILD: 4104 baseline LDCTs; AI as first reader (LungRADS). AI sensitivity was 91.2% vs 89.7% for the human reader, specificity 75.7% vs 90.0%, NPV 99.8% for both, and expected workload reduction was 74.7% [PMID 41308576].
- Walstra et al., 4-IN-THE-LUNG-RUN: 3678 baseline LDCTs; AI first reader. AI produced 31 negative-misclassifications vs 407 for radiologists, and 3/102 missed referrals vs 12/102 [PMID 39754864].
- Lancaster et al., Moscow screening: 283 participants; standalone AI nodule volumetry. AI had 8 negative-misclassifications; workload reduction of up to 86.7% was suggested [PMID 35123156].
- Jiang et al., UKLS: 710 participants, 939 follow-up scans; volume doubling time. AI had a 9.1% 3-month negative misclassification rate vs 18.2-63.6% for humans [PMID 41319449]. Separately, nodule matching succeeded in 83.5% (283/339) of persisting nodules [PMID 42668303]. A further UKLS analysis of 1250 scans found only 1.9% of participants had extra workload from perifissural nodules [PMID 41872344].
- Antonissen et al.: 4146 participants from three European trials; malignancy risk. AUC 0.94 vs 0.93 for PanCan overall, and 0.90 vs 0.86 for indeterminate nodules [PMID 40956165].
- Peeters et al., LUNA25: 468 nodules (463 scans) from three European trials; AI AUC 0.78 vs 0.70 for 65 radiologists [PMID 42340186].
- Cui et al., Chinese program: 360 individuals; detection. DL-CAD sensitivity was 90.1% vs 76.0% for double reading, at 1.0 false positives per scan [PMID 34871936].
- Ji et al., West China Hospital: 259,121 non-high-risk participants; AI with thin-section LDCT. Detection rate was 0.3% vs 0.2%, and 5-year survival 95.4% vs 81.3% [PMID 40213646].
- Mikhael et al. (Sybil): NLST, MGH (8821 LDCTs), and CGMH (12,280 LDCTs); risk prediction. 1-year AUC 0.86-0.94 [PMID 36634294].
- Huang et al.: 2294 PanCan participants; follow-up risk. 1-year AUC 0.968 [PMID 32864596].
- Ardila et al.: 6716 NLST cases and 1139 independent cases; AUC 94.4%, outperforming six radiologists when no prior CT was available [PMID 31110349].
- Trajanovski et al. (NLST, LHMC, Kaggle) reported AUC 86-94% [PMID 33895622]; Venkadesh et al. reported AUC 0.91 and 0.94 on DLCST and MILD subsets [PMID 37526548].

**2) Recurring patterns**

- Cohorts recur: NLST for training, and European trials (DLCST, MILD, NELSON-related, UKLS) for testing [PMID 37526548; 40956165; 42340186].
- Tasks fall into three groups: AI as first reader/triage [PMID 41308576; 39754864; 35123156], nodule malignancy risk [PMID 40956165; 37526548], and growth or tracking [PMID 41319449; 42668303].
- Most designs compare AI with radiologists or the PanCan model, and most are retrospective.

**3) Gaps**

- No study in the context was a prospective trial of AI-assisted screening with mortality as an outcome. Ji et al. is the only one reporting survival, and it was a retrospective cohort [PMID 40213646].
- AI-first-reader work reports workload reductions as estimates, not as measured changes in real practice [PMID 41308576; 35123156].
- Cancer numbers are small in several validations (for example, 9 cancers in UKLS) [PMID 41319449].
- Cost-effectiveness and effects on patient outcomes were not assessed.
- Specificity was lower for AI in BioMILD [PMID 41308576].

38355174.why: This is an RCT protocol for AI in a real screening setting, but it reports no performance results.

41308576.why: It evaluates AI software on 4104 baseline LDCTs from the BioMILD screening trial and reports sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV.

35406501.why: It is a cost-effectiveness Markov model built from literature inputs, with no AI evaluation on screening scans.

33240975.why: It develops and retrospectively evaluates an AI system on LDCT datasets, but not within a defined screening program cohort.

42340186.why: AI was externally tested on baseline scans from three European screening trials and compared with radiologists, with AUC results.

41319449.why: It validates AI volume doubling time assessment on follow-up scans from the UKLS screening trial against expert consensus and histology.

40213646.why: It is a large real-world screening cohort of 259,121 participants comparing AI-assisted LDCT with traditional LDCT on detection rate and survival.

33658025.why: It evaluates AI on LDCT scans from a small retrospective cohort of 117 screening patients, which is not a formal screening program.

42668303.why: It evaluates AI nodule matching in UKLS trial participants and reports the matching success rate.

39165498.why: It is a prospective case-control study with an AI nodule model combined with liquid biopsy, not a screening cohort evaluation of AI.

35123156.why: AI evaluated as standalone reader on baseline ultra-LDCT scans from the Moscow Lung Cancer Screening program, compared with radiologists.

35311112.why: Prospective study validating an AI plus liquid biopsy classifier on nodule patients, but not a screening-program cohort per se.

41749798.why: AI used to design educational modules, not a validated imaging AI.

36672655.why: Clinical trial of AI-assisted nodule detection with sensitivity results, but a small 200-person hospital setting rather than a screening program.

39754864.why: AI first-reader evaluated on 3678 baseline LDCTs from the 4-IN-THE-LUNG-RUN screening trial with performance results.

33482120.why: Secondary analysis of AI risk score on baseline screening CTs (192 studies, weighted), partially a screening cohort but mostly a modeling and cost analysis.

34264825.why: Challenge evaluating algorithms on 100 NLST subjects; screening trial data but small and a challenge format.

32864596.why: Deep learning model validated externally on PanCan screening cohort with AUC results, developed on NLST.

33895622.why: Deep learning risk model trained on NLST and externally validated on LHMC and other screening datasets with AUCs.

36600392.why: Protocol for a screening cohort evaluating AI as reader, but no results yet.

31110349.why: Deep learning model validated on NLST screening trial cases plus an independent clinical set, with reader studies and AUC results.

36909593.why: Model developed and tested on an NLST subset with AUC, but internal data only and no independent validation.

40956165.why: External test of a DL malignancy risk algorithm on pooled European screening trial data (DLCST, MILD, NELSON) with AUC results.

37526548.why: DL algorithm trained on NLST and externally validated on DLCST and MILD screening trial cohorts with AUC results.

34871936.why: DL-CAD evaluated on scans from a real Chinese LDCT screening program, with sensitivity and false-positive rates.

31558626.why: Cardiovascular risk assessment in a screening cohort, with no AI system.

40001094.why: AI-assisted mobile LDCT screening program with detection rates and costs, but no standalone AI performance validation.

36634294.why: Sybil validated on held-out NLST data and on external MGH and CGMH cohorts, with AUC and C-index results.

37489991.why: AI body composition tool applied to NLST scans for risk prediction, not lung cancer detection.

31675322.why: Evaluated on public challenge datasets (LUNA16, Kaggle), not an actual screening program or trial.

42608820.why: Narrative review of cardiovascular screening within LCS; no AI system validated on a screening cohort.

31747155.why: Describes the Moscow screening program and states AI was used for quality control, but the abstract gives no performance results.

41872344.why: Commercial AI nodule detection was evaluated on 1,250 baseline LDCT scans from the UKLS trial, with workload results reported.

39278738.why: Fully automated AI body composition software was applied to a real LCS population (938 volunteers), but the study examines associations rather than validating AI performance for cancer screening.

39709114.why: Evaluates eligibility criteria in the Yorkshire Lung Screening Trial; no AI system is involved.
